newsitem.title: UK: Many UK Channel 5 viewers may need aerials - report.
newsitem.headline: Many UK Channel 5 viewers may need aerials - report.

text.p: As many as four million homes will need new television aerials to be able to clearly pick up Britain's new Channel 5 station when broadcasting begins at the end of March, the Times reported on Friday.

"The bill for the new aerials, which cost from 40 pounds to 200 pounds ($67 to $336) each, could exceed 500 million pounds ($840 million) and will have to be met by viewers," the newspaper said. "Channel 5 is under no obligation to foot the bill."
The report said the station is required under its licence only to retune video recorders so they can receive the channel without interference, and that will cost it 150 million pounds ($252 million).
The newspaper said people living in parts of London and in a number of cities throughout Britain are most likely to need the new aerials.

Channel 5, Britain's fifth terrestrial television network, is a joint venture of British media groups Pearson Plc and United News & Media Plc, U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus and Luxembourg broadcast group CLT.
